project.name: GharHisab
project.idea: Privacy-first, local-first household finance app for Indian families: know what you have, what you owe, what is coming. The phone owns the encrypted financial ledger; the cloud owns only platform operations.

phases.summary: Vision locked: household financial OS; 7 product principles; MVP scope (PRD §5).
Flutter + Spring Boot modular monolith + Next.js admin; 20 sprints / 772 pts / 145 stories; 4 parallel tracks.
PRD, BRD, functional spec, UX spec, 145 user stories with ACs (docs/01–03, user-stories/).
System architecture, HLD/LLD, data model, API spec, security & threat model, 12 ADRs, execution order (docs/04–12, 17, 19, 25).
S0 and S1 closed & accepted (16 stories, 59 tests, 4 goldens). S2 active: GH-020 encrypted ledger landed 2 Oct.

requirements.text: Encrypted local ledger (SQLCipher) — financial data never leaves the phone
Family sharing via end-to-end encrypted sync
On-device auto-capture from SMS and Gmail

sprints.goal: Foundation & tooling: monorepo, flavors, Spring Boot skeleton, admin scaffold, CI, security scans
Design system & app shell: theme, Money, MoneyText/Input, core widgets, bottom nav, routing
Encrypted vault & security: SQLCipher ledger, vault unlock, key management

A.original_requirements: Household financial operating system for Indian families with privacy by architecture.
A.product_goals:
Know what you have
Know what you owe
Know what is coming
Keep control of your financial records
A.user_stories:
As a developer, I want a monorepo (apps/mobile, apps/admin, services/api, packages/*, infrastructure, docs) so that all code lives in one versioned place.
As a developer, I want Flutter project with flavors (dev/staging/prod) and lints so that builds are reproducible.
As a developer, I want Spring Boot 21 modular-monolith skeleton so that backend modules have clear boundaries.
As a developer, I want Next.js admin skeleton (TS, Tailwind, shadcn, TanStack) so that admin work can start in parallel.
As a developer, I want docker-compose for Postgres, Redis, LocalStack so that backend runs locally without AWS.
As a developer, I want CI pipelines (mobile, admin, api) with privacy gate so that regressions and privacy leaks are blocked.
As a developer, I want Fastlane to TestFlight + Play internal track so that real phones get builds from sprint 1.
As a developer, I want shared design tokens package (JSON → Dart + Tailwind) so that mobile and admin stay visually consistent.

adrs.title: ADR-001: Flutter for customer mobile
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Flutter + Dart.  
**Reason:** Strong cross-platform rendering consistency, mature mobile tooling, and a good fit for the 47-screen UI-heavy product.

adrs.title: ADR-002: Local financial source of truth
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Encrypted on-device SQLite is authoritative.  
**Reason:** Privacy, offline-first behavior, reduced breach blast radius, and clear product trust model.

adrs.title: ADR-003: SQLCipher
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Encrypt the local SQLite database.  
**Reason:** Financial records are sensitive even when the device filesystem is protected.

adrs.title: ADR-004: Spring Boot modular monolith
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Start modular.  
**Reason:** Lower operational complexity and easier transactional/authorization reasoning.

adrs.title: ADR-005: PostgreSQL operational-only
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** PostgreSQL stores platform metadata, not the customer financial ledger.  
**Reason:** Enforces the privacy boundary structurally.

adrs.title: ADR-006: Deterministic financial engines
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Money calculations are code-owned, not LLM-owned.  
**Reason:** Reproducibility, auditability, and correctness.

adrs.title: ADR-007: Local vault unlock independent of cloud auth
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Biometric/PIN unlocks a device key; Cognito governs only online operations.  
**Reason:** Offline-first; expired tokens must never block access to the user's own ledger.

adrs.title: ADR-008: Family sharing via end-to-end encrypted sync (Accepted 2026-10-01)
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Each member has their own phone and local vault. Shared records sync phone-to-phone as E2EE envelopes (space keys wrapped per device); the server relays ciphertext with a 30-day TTL and holds no keys. The family head controls which spaces each member can see. Full spec: `22_FAMILY_SHARING.md`.  
**Reason:** Product owner requirement (no shared phones; head controls visibility, e.g. children see school fees but not EMIs).  
**Privacy note:** This is data category 4 ("explicitly consented cloud financial data", `16_ROADMAP.md`) in **ciphertext-only** form. It amends CLAUDE.md §5 narrowly: no plaintext financial data, no relational financial columns, no admin visibility, ciphertext stored outside PostgreSQL with TTL.

adrs.title: ADR-009: User-controlled encrypted backup file
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** `.ghbackup` (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM) saved wherever the user chooses; no server copy.  
**Reason:** Mitigates device-loss data loss without creating a server ledger.

adrs.title: ADR-010: Stateless AI gateway
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Cloud LLM calls pass through a zero-retention gateway with per-request consent and aggregate-only context.  
**Reason:** Keeps provider keys off-device while preserving the privacy boundary.

adrs.title: ADR-011: On-device auto-capture from SMS and Gmail (Accepted 2026-10-01)
adrs.decision:
**Decision:** Android reads bank SMS under Play's SMS-based money management exception; Gmail is read via on-device OAuth (`gmail.readonly`). All parsing, de-duplication and categorisation happen on the phone; raw messages are not stored or uploaded. iOS uses Gmail + import fallbacks. Spec: `23_AUTO_CAPTURE.md`.  
**Reason:** Manual entry fatigue is the top retention risk; on-device capture keeps the privacy model intact.

**ADR-011 addendum (iOS):** iPhone uses a Shortcuts Message-trigger automation calling our App Intent, plus email (Gmail/Outlook/IMAP), share-sheet and family Android capture. Prototype in Phase 4.

adrs.title: ADR-012: SQLCipher-format ledger via SQLite3MultipleCiphers (Accepted 2026-10-02, GH-020)
adrs.decision:
**Context:** CLAUDE.md §4/§15 require Drift over SQLCipher. Since drift 2.32 / `sqlite3` 3.x, `sqlcipher_flutter_libs` is no longer supported; Drift's documented path bundles SQLite3MultipleCiphers (sqlite3mc) through `sqlite3` build hooks.
**Decision:** Bundle sqlite3mc (`hooks.user_defines.sqlite3.source: sqlite3mc` in `apps/mobile/pubspec.yaml`) and run it in **SQLCipher v4 mode** (`PRAGMA cipher='sqlcipher'; PRAGMA legacy=4`) before `PRAGMA key`. The key is 256 random bits from `Random.secure()`, stored in iOS Keychain (`unlocked_this_device`, not synchronizable) / Android Keystore-backed storage, never derived from a password or PIN, never transmitted. The opener refuses to run if the cipher is not linked, never deletes a file on a *wrong* key, and resets the ledger only when the key is *missing* (reinstall/wipe — recovery only via `.ghbackup`, ADR-009).
**Reason:** Keeps the SQLCipher on-disk format and cipher (AES-256-CBC + HMAC-SHA512, PBKDF2-SHA512) the architecture specifies, on the maintained library path, and lets host-side `flutter test` exercise the real encryption (open-without-key test).
**Consequences:** iOS/Android build the native library from source via hooks (no CocoaPods/Gradle step). A future switch to sqlite3mc's default ChaCha20 scheme would be a rekey migration (GH-021) with its own ADR.
